purpose: Refactor monolithic 568-line app/src/index.ts into 13 single-responsibility subscriber modules and 2 utility files, reducing the entry point to 42 lines.
riskRationale: Pure structural refactoring with no business logic changes. All handler functions are reused as-is, tests pass, lint is clean, and the event-driven semantics are preserved exactly. Only minor documentation and code-quality issues remain.

text: Well-executed decomposition that faithfully preserves all existing logic. Each subscriber is a focused factory function with structured error handling, shared utilities are properly extracted to dedicated modules, and the entry point now cleanly orchestrates initialization. A handful of minor issues — JSDoc documentation regressions on 5 public APIs, dead fallback code, an unnecessary guard, an unused variable, and inconsistent signal propagation — are easy to address and do not affect correctness.

reasoning: All changes are faithful to the original logic, all imports resolve, all tests pass, and the architecture is sound. Remaining issues are documentation and code-quality nits that do not affect functionality.

message: Reduced from 568 to 42 lines — now only orchestrates initialization: env validation, core service creation, subscriber registration, webhook handler, and SIGTERM cleanup. This is the ideal role of an entry point.

Central router cleanly composes all subscribers, mixing factory-created and lib-instantiated subscribers (FeedbackSubscriber, MetaReviewSubscriber) in a single registration call with clear dependency injection.
Replaced the original dynamic import() in the inline ReplySubscriber with a static import — removes a code smell and enables better bundler/tree-shaking support.
Clean extraction of getToken() with a meaningful error message when GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, replacing the silent '' fallback.
Shared buildConfig() and parseEnvInt() extracted cleanly, eliminating duplication across all subscribers.
Consistent error handling pattern with structured Logger usage across all subscribers — errors include repo and context, never swallow or expose internals.

Good separation: simple command-handler subscribers use lightweight factory functions while richer lib-dependent subscribers (FeedbackSubscriber, MetaReviewSubscriber) are instantiated directly, keeping factory APIs focused.
JSDoc removed from getToken() — the original had a doc comment documenting the function. Project conventions require JSDoc for public functions.
suggestion: Restore the JSDoc comment that existed on the original function.

message: registerSubscribers() is a public function exported from this module but has no JSDoc. Per the project conventions, all public functions should be documented with JSDoc.
suggestion: Add JSDoc describing the function's purpose, parameters, and return value.

message: Dead code in previousHeadSha fallback. For pr.synchronize events, GitHub sends 'before' at the root of the webhook payload, not inside pull_request. The pull_request?.before fallback will always be undefined.
suggestion: Remove the pull_request?.before fallback since it will never produce a value.

message: event.prNumber || 0 and event.repo are repeated in both the event payload and the publish call payload. Minor duplication.
suggestion: Reuse the resolved prNumber and repo variables instead of re-reading event.prNumber and event.repo in the bus.publish() call.

message: Feature-enabled check (line 33) is evaluated after mention parsing (lines 21-23). When config.conversation.enabled is false, the subscriber still parses the comment body and checks for @mentions on every comment.created/review_comment.created event before eventually short-circuiting.
suggestion: Move the enabled guard to the top of the handle function, before any parsing or mention detection, to avoid unnecessary work when the feature is disabled.

message: Unused variable _parentId — computed but never referenced. The underscore prefix suppresses the TypeScript lint warning, but the API call and computation are wasted.

Each subscriber factory creates its own new Logger('App') instance. In the original code, a single logger was shared. This results in N loggers named 'App' making it impossible to distinguish which subscriber logged a message.
suggestion: Rename each logger to its subscriber name (e.g., Logger('AnalyzeSubscriber')) for better observability in logs.

message: Inconsistent AbortSignal propagation: analyze.ts, audit.ts, and explain.ts do not pass 'signal' to their handler functions, while auto-analyze.ts, fix.ts, review.ts, and conversation.ts do. This means cancellation requests are ignored for the /analyze, /audit, and /explain commands.
suggestion: Pass 'signal' to all handler calls for consistent cancellation support, matching the pattern used in auto-analyze.ts and fix.ts.

message: Unnecessary null guard on required factory parameter. The createDiscoverSubscriber signature requires LearningStore (non-optional), so a null/undefined value is a programming error that should throw rather than silently return.
suggestion: Remove the if (!learningStore) guard — the TypeScript type already guarantees its presence.
